name: Our Lady of Lourdes
history: On 11 February 1858 a lady in white appeared to Bernadette Soubirous, a poor girl of fourteen, at the grotto of Massabielle near Lourdes in the Pyrenees. In eighteen appearances she asked for prayer and penance, and on 25 March named herself: ‘I am the Immaculate Conception.’ The Church approved the apparitions in 1862, and Lourdes became one of the great places of pilgrimage, especially for the sick.
life: Bernadette’s family were so poor that they lived in a former jail. She was gathering firewood with her sister and a friend when she saw the lady in a hollow of the rock. In the following weeks crowds came with her, though only she saw the lady. On 25 February, told to drink at the spring, she scraped at the muddy ground until water came; the spring has flowed ever since, and of the many cures reported there the Church has recognised a small number as miraculous after strict medical examination. Questioned again and again by clergy and officials, Bernadette never changed her account. She did not know what the words Immaculate Conception meant, but they convinced her parish priest. In 1862 the bishop of Tarbes declared that the faithful were justified in believing. Lourdes is approved private revelation: Catholics are not bound to believe it, but the Church finds in it nothing contrary to faith.
prayerTo: Our Lady of Lourdes, you came to a poor and sickly girl and called the world to prayer and penance. Pray for all the sick, for those who care for them, and for all who come to you on pilgrimage. Pray for me, that I may come to the spring of grace your Son has opened, and be healed in body and soul as He wills. Amen.
penance: Today is the World Day of the Sick. Visit or telephone someone who is ill, or offer one of your own pains for them, and pray a decade of the Rosary, as Bernadette did at the grotto.
meditation: The lady told Bernadette that she did not promise to make her happy in this world, but in the next. What are you asking of God that He may wish to give in another way?
